title: The coordinate-specified dual tautological linearization and vector orbit morphism
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $G$ be a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme], and let $I$ be a finite set. Let $\rho:G\to\operatorname{GL}(k^I)$ be a homomorphism of group schemes [def-sc-general-linear-group]. Let $Y$ be a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $j:Y\to\mathbf P_{\mathrm{lines}}(k^I)$ a morphism. Put $L=j^*\mathcal O(1)$, using the dual tautological twist [def-pc-projective-space-twist] and module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], and write $s_i=j^*T_i$ for its coordinate sections. A linearized embedding datum consists of an algebraic left $G$-action $a$ on $Y$ and a linearization $D$ of $L$ [def-sfb-group-scheme-linearization] such that for every test $k$-scheme $T$, every $g\in G(T)$, $x\in Y(T)$ and $i\in I$,
$$D(g,x)(x^*s_i)=\sum_{l\in I}\rho(g^{-1})_{il}(gx)^*s_l.$$
Here the matrix entries are the pullbacks of the coordinate functions on $\operatorname{GL}(k^I)$. This formula specifies both equivariance of $j$ and the induced dual tautological linearization. For a $k$-vector space $V$ with basis $b=(b_i)_{i\in I}$ and $y\in Y(k)$, a vector $v\in V$ lifts $j(y)$ if there is an isomorphism $e:y^*L\simeq k$ such that $e(y^*s_i)=b_i^\vee(v)$ for every $i$. For such a based representation define its vector orbit morphism $\alpha_v:G\to\mathbf A^I_k$ [def-nagata-relative-affine-space] by the coordinate functions
$$\alpha_v^*T_i=\sum_{l\in I}\rho_{il}\, b_l^\vee(v).$$
The affine space is the spectrum of $\operatorname{Sym}_k V^\vee$ in the chosen basis. All actions and line maps are tested on arbitrary schemes, including nonreduced schemes. These constructions are defined for arbitrary $j$; the term embedding applies when $j$ is a closed immersion.
